newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Foreign minister says Rwanda ready to retaliate.
newsitem.headline: Foreign minister says Rwanda ready to retaliate.

text.p: Rwandan Foreign Minister Anastase Gasana denied reports on Friday that his government's troops were fighting in Zaire, but said they were ready to hit back against Zairean shelling.

"If we continue to receive such provocations, such attacks on the part of the Zairean army, we have the right to defend ourselves and to engage in defensive action against the Zairean army if that continues," he told Belgian radio.
Reports from the Rwandan town of Gisenyl quoted diplomats saying Rwandan troops have already entered the eastern Zaire town of Goma by lake and land to assist Tutsi rebels fighting to capture it.
He said Rwandan troops were prepared to act if Zairean weapons were used to attack Rwanda.

"If the Rwandan army manages to locate the arms which are destroying the town of Gisenyi from Goma we will not hesitate to take dispositions to destroy those arms which are firing on our population," he said.
Gasana said the fighting in Zaire was an internal affair.
"It is nothing to do with us," he said. "It is an internal conflict.
He said Zaire was firing shells at Rwanda to prevent Rwandan refugees from returning home.
Zaire accused Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda of sending troops into eastern Zaire to wage war against the Zairean army.
Rwanda sent some soldiers into the eastern town of Bukavu earlier this week on a brief overnight incursion which a government troops officer said was aimed at stopping Zaire firing into Rwanda.
